items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: I wouldn't get on that Dan Ryan Express.

ctx.x: Was there ever lessons learned of things not to do?

Oh yes. You know a lot has been written about alcohol and drugs in the jazz community. And I really feel that it has been overblown. And I sometimes wonder whether or not it’s been used early on to kind of discredit the importance of jazz as an art form. Because that © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-

was some of the stuff that early people say oh that music was born in the brothels and houses of ill repute. And it’s funny because when I first started saying I wanted to play jazz I told my father that I wanted to play jazz, because he liked that I was playing the violin, and he said, “Oh I don’t particularly like the idea of you playing jazz because you’ll be in those clubs where all those people are drinking and this, that and the other.” I said, “Daddy, that’s not why I want to play jazz.
